source.title: Unified Neural Network Scaling Laws and Scale-time Equivalence

record.file_problem: None; the full paper and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests error trends across model scale, epochs, and data volume, and argues that double descent is conditional on noise-feature learning rather than inevitable; its reported scale curves include cases that do not show the claimed fall-rise-fall shape.
record.gate_note: The paper also reports scale-time trade-offs and that larger models can require less data to generalize. Those results do not by themselves measure the claim versions' specified error-curve shapes. Numeric values for the error curves are not stated in the text and are available only in figures.
record.test_reason: The study derives conditions for double descent and reports U-shaped model-size curves that contradict a necessary second descent. Its noise comparisons alone do not establish epoch-wise double descent or that adding samples raises error.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors propose scale-time equivalence and explain model-wise double descent through the relative acquisition times of signal and noise. They report that larger overparameterized models can perform worse and that label-noise penalties persist over size and time but are localized over sample count. They do not establish that adding samples causes the localized error increases described in the record.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a random-subspace theoretical model, linear-model error analysis, and vision experiments with CNNs and MLPs; it does not reproduce the original sources' methods.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported behavior varies with dataset and axis. The paper states that Adam's epochs-to-generalization trend first decreases and then increases with scale, unlike the reported SGD scale-time trade-off; it also says scale-wise double descent depends on dataset, model, and label noise.

fits_no_version.finding: Adding label noise produces persistent or growing error differences over epochs and model scale, but localized differences over sample count.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The effect of label noise on test error depends on the scaling axis; an error difference between noise conditions does not itself establish double descent or more-data harm.

record.problems: The relevant error curves are reported in figures without numeric values in the text. The empirical tests cover vision datasets and CNN/MLP architectures, and the authors state that findings do not cover the language domain. Some textual summaries do not specify which plotted noise condition produces each curve shape.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted under the 60-row limit. Figures 2–3 and the scale-time prediction experiments are not included because they report scale-time trade-offs or prediction performance, not the error-curve behavior specified by the claim versions.

untested.parts: The empirical text does not locate the reported U-shaped curves relative to a measured interpolation threshold.
The empirical fall-rise-fall trajectories cannot be determined from the supplied figure captions; the theoretical mechanism is analyzed.
The supplied text does not establish an empirical increase caused by adding samples near an identified interpolation threshold.
The empirical counterexamples concern neural networks; extension across other model classes is not empirically established.
No single effective-complexity measure is shown to predict peak locations across model size, epochs, and samples. Scale-time equivalence alone does not establish this.
Triple or multiple descent and disappearance under optimally tuned regularization are not tested.
No replotting demonstrates conversion of a second descent into an ordinary U-shaped curve. The cube-root parameter proxy does not establish this.

missing.what: The theoretical temporal error decomposition and conditional double-descent trajectories are absent from the rows. They distinguish noise-first learning from signal-first learning.
missing.locator: Section 5.1, Equation 9 and Figure 4; Section 5.2, Equation 10

missing.what: Figure 9 includes unrecorded model-size trajectories for MNIST and additional architecture/dataset combinations across all three axes. Their shapes require the graphical plots; captions alone cannot establish verdicts.
Separate the empirical curves by noise condition and report the fixed sample count, training duration, or model size for each axis. Current rows pool conditions and leave these controls unspecified.
missing.locator: Figure 6; Appendix D, Figure 9; Appendix C.4

record.verdict_notes: Only the supplied text was assessed. Figure captions do not expose the plotted values. Remove both V3 verdicts: neither localized noise penalties nor their disappearance at high sample counts establishes support or a scope limit for more-data harm. Remove the empirical V2 scope verdict because failure to describe a curve is not evidence that it fails.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not establish a fall-rise-fall curve around an explicitly identified interpolation threshold across all tested models or settings.
The text describes noise-related error changes over epochs but does not report that the full fall-rise-fall shape occurs, or establish its location relative to a threshold.
The text reports localized increases with data volume under label noise, but does not give numeric error changes or locate each increase relative to an interpolation threshold.
No systematic test across model classes of risk falling again as capacity passes interpolation.
The paper uses effective parameter count and a scale-time product for predictions, but does not test whether one effective-complexity measure predicts peak location on every axis.
Label-noise effects are tested. The paper does not test triple or multiple descent, or whether optimally tuned regularization eliminates the peak.
The paper uses a cube-root parameter-count proxy but does not show that replotting against an appropriate effective parameter count turns second descent into an ordinary U-shaped curve.
